record.label: production-branch reference; deployment unverified
record.scope: The two units in appliesTo declare ENCORE in this production reference: Minccino (1 star) and Cinccino (2 stars), both NORMAL + FIELD + SOUND, maxPP 80, range 1, no passive. ENCORE has no effect of its own: it re-runs the strategy of another ability, so its actual behaviour on a given cast is that copied ability's behaviour with the Minccino / Cinccino caster. The copied abilities were NOT analysed here (routing uncertainty RUNTIME_ABILITY_DISPATCH).

dispatch.strategy: EncoreStrategy extends AbilityStrategy (defined in abilities.ts, not in its own file)
dispatch.runtimeDispatch: process() looks up AbilityStrategies[lastAbilityUsed] at run time and calls its process(); which strategy that is depends on the fight

record.summary: Repeat the team's last copyable ability. On cast the caster runs the base process (spends PP, ult counter +1, default animation, appends its own skill, ENCORE, to its team's history list). It then takes its team's history list (the list of skills that went through AbilityStrategy.process for that team in this fight), picks the most recent entry that is not in InimitableAbilities (findLast), and, if there is one, calls that ability's strategy process with the Encore caster, the same cast target and the same crit flag. If there is none (nothing copyable has been cast by the team yet) only the base process happens. Because the copied process is run by the Encore caster, its star-indexed numbers, AP, range and positions are the Minccino / Cinccino caster's, not those of the unit that originally cast it.

targeting.who: inherited: the cast target passed to the strategy is forwarded unchanged to the copied ability, whose own targeting rules then decide who is affected
targeting.note: Encore does not consult the copied strategy's requiresTarget / canCritByDefault; the cast uses Encore's own flags (requiresTarget true, no default crit)

effects.scaling: no numbers of its own. The copied process receives the Encore caster, so star tables, AP scaling, held items, passives and positions are read from the Minccino / Cinccino entity; the crit flag is the one rolled for the Encore cast (ENCORE canCritByDefault is false, so crit needs an ABILITY_CRIT effect; the copied strategy's own canCritByDefault is not consulted). Table entries for 1 and 2 stars are the ones that apply.
effects.resolution: The copied strategy calls its own super.process, so for a copied ability that does: PP is reduced a second time (min(0)(pp - maxPP); PP above maxPP from overflow can be removed), the ult counter increases a second time (2 per Encore cast in total), a second default animation broadcast is made, and the caster's own skill, ENCORE, is appended to the history a second time (the copied ability itself is never appended, since the list stores pokemon.skill of the caster). Whether a particular copied ability skips these (preventDefaultAnim, no super call) depends on that ability and was not traced.

The list is per simulation and per team (blue or red) and is never cleared in the files read; entries are skills of casters (including casters that have since died) in cast order. Only calls to AbilityStrategy.process append to it. ENCORE and the other InimitableAbilities (METRONOME, MIMIC, SKETCH, ASSIST, KNOWLEDGE_THIEF, SKILL_SWAP, HIDDEN_POWER_*, ...) are skipped by the search, and abilities executed through a copy (Encore, Metronome and similar) leave the copier's skill, not the copied one, in the list. The most recent copyable entry is therefore the most recent cast by any unit of the team whose own skill is copyable. Ties do not exist (a single list).

starBehavior.note: Encore has no star table; the copied ability's star-indexed values use the Encore caster's stars (1 for Minccino, 2 for Cinccino)

record.positionalConditions: None of Encore's own; whatever positional conditions the copied ability has apply with the Encore caster's position and the forwarded target.
record.repeatedCastsAndModes: Each cast re-reads the team's history, so the copied ability changes as other units cast. Consecutive Encore casts do not copy each other (ENCORE is inimitable), so the second Encore copies the same ability as the first unless another copyable cast happened in between. An Encore cast with no earlier copyable team cast does nothing beyond the base process.
record.rawVsResolved: No declared numbers. Requested / applied amounts are those of the copied ability evaluated for the Encore caster (its own record, if one exists, says how, but with the Minccino / Cinccino stars); extra PP removal and a second ult count come from the nested super.process.
dependsOnUnverifiedGenericCombat: When the cast fires in a real fight (PP gain, silence, canCast): only the pp >= maxPP && canCast gate and castAbility were read
Every copied ability's own behaviour: not analysed here; see that ability's record or the shared references
unresolved: Routing uncertainty RUNTIME_ABILITY_DISPATCH is the point of this ability: the effect depends on whichever ability the team cast last, so no single behaviour can be stated; each copied ability must be read separately

Whether a copied ability that reads pokemon.skill, pokemon.passive or the unit's identity (for example forms or passives keyed to the original caster) behaves differently when run by Minccino / Cinccino was not traced
Copied abilities that need a target of a kind other than the forwarded cast target, or that require requiresTarget false, were not examined

Whether a copied strategy's own super.process always runs (and so doubles PP removal, ult count and animation) was only traced for the base class; strategies that call it with preventDefaultAnim or skip it were not enumerated

Minccino and Cinccino are the only units listed for this identifier; the team history only counts casts that went through AbilityStrategy.process (other cast paths, if any, were not searched beyond git grep of the two list names)
No pinned-helper probe was run for this record; the code was read, not executed
